## Terraform Provider for SAP Integration Suite v0.2.0

### Overview

0.2.0 is the first release that works against a real SAP Integration Suite
tenant. 0.1.0 was built from documentation research alone and could not
authenticate under Terraform. This release fixes that, and fixes what the
first acceptance runs against a tenant turned up on 2026-09-26. The wire
contracts were also checked against the services' own `$metadata`
documents and against SAP's automation tooling.

Several resources sent property names that SAP's entities do not have.
Correcting them changes a few schemas, so read "Upgrading from 0.1.0" before
you run `terraform plan`.

### Highlights

- **Working authentication.** 0.1.0 built its OAuth client with the context
  of the provider's configure call. Terraform cancels that context as soon as
  the call returns, so every request failed with `context canceled` on the
  token URL. Tokens are now fetched independently of that call, with a
  60-second limit per request.
- **Externalized integration flow parameters.**
  `sapintegrationsuite_integration_flow_configuration` sets the parameters
  you list, keeps each parameter's data type and rejects unknown keys before
  writing anything. Together with the new `redeploy_triggers` on the
  deployment, new values reach the runtime in the same apply.
- **Explicit design-time versions.** `save_as_version` on integration flows,
  message mappings and script collections saves the uploaded content under
  the version you name. Uploading content alone does not change an
  artifact's version, and deployments only redeploy when the version changes.
- **Deployments that fail stay visible.** A deployment that SAP accepted but
  that did not start in time, or ended in `ERROR`, is kept in state and
  marked tainted. Earlier it was dropped from state and kept running on the
  tenant, where `terraform destroy` could no longer reach it.
- **Secure parameters and full number range management.** Secure parameters
  are managed with a write-only value. Number ranges can now be read,
  imported and destroyed; a tenant confirmed the `GET` and `DELETE` that SAP
  does not document.

### New resources

- `sapintegrationsuite_integration_flow_configuration`
- `sapintegrationsuite_secure_parameter`
- `sapintegrationsuite_business_data_graph` (experimental)

### New data sources

- `sapintegrationsuite_access_policy_runtime_assignments`: the runtimes an
  access policy is replicated to, with SAP's transfer status.
- `sapintegrationsuite_business_data_graph` (experimental)

### Upgrading from 0.1.0

0.1.0 could not send a single request to SAP, so it cannot have created or
imported anything. The upgrade therefore changes configuration only;
attributes that were removed are dropped from state on the first refresh.

| Resource or data source | Change to make |
|---|---|
| `sapintegrationsuite_integration_package` | Add the new required `short_text`. SAP rejects a package without it. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_access_policy_reference` | Add the new required `name`. Use SAP's constants: `INTEGRATION_FLOW` instead of `IntegrationFlow`, `exactString` instead of `EQUALS`. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_integration_adapter` and data source | Remove `type` and `application`; the entity has neither. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_service_endpoints` data source | Read `api_definitions[*].name` instead of `api_definitions[*].type`. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_partner_authorized_user` and data source | Write `user` in lowercase; SAP stores it lowercased. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_api_product` | Set `api_proxy_names`, now required. Every attribute now forces a new product, because SAP answers every update with 405. |
| `sapintegrationsuite_access_policy` and data source | Remove references to `reconciliation_status`; use the runtime assignments data source. |
| Keystore entry data sources | `valid_not_before` / `valid_not_after` are now RFC 3339 timestamps. |

For example, an access policy reference:

```terraform
resource "sapintegrationsuite_access_policy_reference" "order_flows" {
  access_policy_id = sapintegrationsuite_access_policy.order_team.id
  name             = "Order intake flow"   # new, required
  artifact_type    = "INTEGRATION_FLOW"    # was "IntegrationFlow"
  attribute        = "Name"
  operator         = "exactString"         # was "EQUALS"
  value            = "ORDER_INTAKE"
}
```

The provider rejects the old constants at plan time and names the
replacement.

### SAP API corrections

These were found on a tenant and are fixed without any change on your side:

- SAP answers several successful writes with `200` or `202` and no body
  (content updates, `SaveAsVersion`, credential, Partner Directory and
  access policy creates). The provider now reads the object back. Earlier it
  failed on the empty body, and the next apply then failed because the
  object already existed.
- Integration package updates use `PUT` (SAP answers `PATCH` with 501) and
  keep the package's version, vendor and tags, which a bare `PUT` resets.
- Integration flows and message mappings exported under a different ID can
  be updated: the provider aligns `Bundle-SymbolicName` with the artifact ID
  in the uploaded copy, because SAP rejects any update that changes it.
- Certificates: untrusted and self-signed certificates can be imported
  (`fingerprintVerified=true`), and existing ones replaced (`update=true`).
- API products and key value maps: SAP returns links as `__deferred`
  objects, which the provider now follows instead of failing to decode.
- `data.sapintegrationsuite_partner` filters the partner list instead of
  reading by key, which SAP does not support.

### Experimental

`sapintegrationsuite_business_data_graph` targets API Composition's
Configuration API with separate credentials (`provider.api_composition`,
service plan `configuration`). SAP shows no request body for updates and no
delete request, and the resource has not been run against a live system.
Expect schema changes before it is promoted.

### Known limitations

- `runtime_location_id` routes requests to an Edge Integration Cell through
  `/location/<id>/api/v1`. It has never been tested against a tenant with an
  Edge Integration Cell and is not supported. Leave it unset.
- Reading, deleting and importing number ranges, and the secure parameter
  entity set, use operations that SAP does not document but that worked on a
  tenant in September 2026.
- There is no API proxy resource yet. Value mapping entries, certificate
  chains, known hosts and PGP keyrings are not implemented.

### Compatibility

- Terraform 1.5 or later; 1.11 or later for resources with write-only
  secrets (`*_wo` attributes).
- Terraform plugin protocol 6.
